questions.q: In Helm vocabulary, what is a "release"?
options: A tagged version of a container image
A named, tracked instance of a chart installed into a cluster with a specific set of values
The GitHub tag applied when a chart is published
A synonym for Chart.yaml
questions.explain: A release is what you get when you install a chart: a named, tracked deployment of that chart with particular values applied. Charts are templates; releases are running instances of them.

questions.q: Northbridge's product-catalog chart is installed in both staging and production. What is the correct way to give each environment different replica counts and image tags from the same chart?
options: Maintain two separate copies of the templates/ directory, one per environment
Edit the rendered manifests by hand after helm install finishes
Pass a different values file (e.g. --values values-staging.yaml vs --values values-prod.yaml) against the same unchanged templates
Helm does not support multiple environments from one chart
questions.explain: Templates stay identical across environments; only the values file supplied at install or upgrade time changes, which is exactly the parameterization Helm is designed for.

questions.q: What does helm upgrade do differently from simply deleting and reinstalling a release?
options: It is functionally identical to delete-then-reinstall
It compares the new chart/values against the currently running release and applies only what changed, recording the change as a new revision
It only updates the values.yaml file without touching the cluster
It requires Tiller to be running in the cluster
questions.explain: helm upgrade performs an incremental change against the running release and records it as a new numbered revision, rather than tearing everything down and recreating it from scratch.

questions.q: A bad helm upgrade just went out to the catalog release. What is the fastest correct way to undo it?
options: Manually locate the previous YAML files and kubectl apply them one by one
helm rollback catalog <previous-revision-number>
helm uninstall catalog, then wait and hope Kubernetes restores the old state
Delete the Pods and let the ReplicaSet recreate them
questions.explain: Because every install/upgrade is a recorded revision, helm rollback reapplies a prior revision's manifests and values in a single command — the atomic rollback hand-maintained YAML never had.

questions.q: What is the relationship between a chart and a release?
options: They are the same thing, just two names for one object
A chart is a reusable, versioned package of templates and defaults; a release is a specific running instance of that chart with values applied
A release is the source package, and a chart is the running instance
A chart can only ever produce exactly one release in a given cluster
questions.explain: The chart is the reusable template package. Installing it produces a release — a named, tracked, running instance — and the same chart can produce multiple independent releases (e.g. one per environment).
